summary: What worked: shortening the sliding-window attention in the S layers from 1024 to 256 (one line; the dataloader packs multiple independent documents per 2048-token row, so long-range attention is mostly across unrelated docs) gave 0.988763 -> 0.987049 on a3's 2**18-batch base, and stacking a4's shallow depth-6 shape with my widening to dim 768 gave 0.978654, the cell best. What did not: head_dim 128->64 (1.003634, worse), deleting all but one full-context layer (SSSSSSSL, 0.988363), and widening past dim 768 to 896 (0.984430) - the width curve turns there. I also measured the cell's replicate noise: two byte-identical configs scored 0.986614 and 0.987748, so sd ~0.0008 and single-run gaps under ~0.002 are not resolved. Next I would test 6d26886 + WARMDOWN_RATIO 1.0 and + the prefetch dataloader (both worth ~-0.0006 each at dim 640), and re-run the batch ladder (2**19 vs 2**18) at the new depth-6/dim-768 shape, since the optimal tokens-per-step likely moved with the shape.
